name: Muslim Legal Fund of America
mission: MLFA is a community-centric grassroots non-profit organization fighting for national security reform, upholding and establishing justice in our courtrooms and communities for Muslims in America. MLFA is the leading nonprofit legal fund dedicated to defending Muslims’ civil rights and liberties at the federal level.
theoryOfChange: The Muslim Legal Fund of America (MLFA) has a '2021 Strategic Plan Brief' which outlines their vision, mission, guiding principles, core beliefs, and strategic priorities. This document describes their approach as 'Turning charitable donations into legal services for select cases with potential civil liberties impact, sometimes known as impact litigation'. Their strategic priorities include strengthening and protecting the Muslim nonprofit community, preventing unwarranted indictments, and increasing the reach and effect of impact litigation. MLFA aims to advance equality and justice for American Muslim organizations and individuals by combating injustices done in the name of national security.

Since its <cite id="2">founding in 2001</cite>, the organization has specialized in complex legal challenges including <cite id="3">terrorism-related criminal defense, civil litigation, and immigration matters</cite>. In FY2024, the charity managed <cite id="4">total revenue of $4,046,006</cite>, reflecting a steady <cite id="5">three-year revenue growth rate of 8.1%</cite>. MLFA distinguishes itself by funding the Constitutional Law Center for Muslims in America, a nonprofit law firm that provides direct representation. Their work has led to significant legal victories, such as <cite id="6">winning acquittals in terrorism cases</cite> and successfully <cite id="7">removing individuals from the No Fly List</cite>. Beyond individual defense, the organization strengthens the sector by providing <cite id="8">training for nonprofit leaders and lawyers</cite>, reaching over 500 professionals in 2022 alone. This dual focus on high-stakes litigation and community capacity building addresses a unique niche in the civil rights landscape.
